name: Dr. Alexander Hoffmann
headline: Snr. Industry Manager & Data Strategy Lead at Google
summary: Artificial intelligence fundamentally changes how marketing works. I help companies to not get lost in this brave new world where your data and AI capabilities make all the difference.

positions.title: Senior Industry Manager & Data Strategy Lead
Industry Manager & Data Strategy Lead
positions.description:
Industry Manager // 
I am a growth advisor for online marketplaces and lead generation companies in Central Europe. The verticals I focus on are mostly real estate and finance.

Data Strategy Lead //
Data, analytics, and machine learning are the new frontier of marketing. However, when you look at how marketers are using big data, it typically plays out in one of three ways – big dumb data, big scary data, or big useful data. I advise companies to ensure that their big data targeting efforts understand consumer intent and make big data be a meaningful input to making a relevant customer experience.

I have also founded Google's Data Strategy School, which helps my colleagues (and me) not get lost in this brave new world.

Keynote Speaker // 
Speaker at Global Online Marketplace Summit in Miami, Property Portal Watch conference in Bangkok and Madrid, International Classifieds Marketplace Conference in Budapest (among others).

20% Project //
I still try to help when (especially my Google Hardware) colleagues have questions about finding the right customer (e.g., for the Google Pixel smartphone).

positions.title: Industry Manager
positions.description:
Still advising digitally native brands to grow in Central Europe. Finally know what I am doing.

In addition: the in-house consulting role got formalized to a proper 20% project. Supported the launch of the Pixel 3 smartphone in Germany.

positions.title: Associate Industry Manager
positions.description:
Stayed in the same team, but changed country and responsibility, extended scope of the role. 

In addition: I started to consult our own marketing teams (e.g. Google Hardware).

positions.title: Key Account Manager (PurePlay)
positions.description: Switched teams and helped digitally native brands to grow.

positions.title: Key Account Manager (Media & Entertainment)
positions.description: I helped a number of key clients in the media & entertainment industry, which included international video on demand/streaming, audio distribution, and gaming companies.

positions.title: Consultant - Digital Strategy & Transformation
positions.description: I advised companies on their digital strategy. Topics close to my heart were lean methodologies, business model generation approaches, and minimum viable products. The industries I've spent the most time on were automotive and pharma.

positions.title: Intern - Account Management
positions.description: For the first time, I was allowed to manage a marketing campaign for an international automotive manufacturer. In my role, I navigated between us (the agency) and the client, trying to navigate what we could do and what was expected of us.

positions.title: Co-Founder & CMO
positions.description:
Together with a good friend from University, I founded the e-learning platform Video Tutor. We helped schools integrate e-learning into the classroom in a way that truly complements their teachers' work.

We did this by combining world-class content with powerful analytics and administrative features that let teachers do everything – from assigning homework to communicating with parents – online. This enabled teachers to spend more time on what really matters: Helping students to perform at their best.

The platform got rebranded to http://thinkhubble.io/ in 2016. Powered by publishing house Ernst Klett.

positions.title: Co-Founder & CMO
positions.description:
After my studies, I founded an eCommerce platform with a shopping cart price comparison engine at its core. We helped customers find the lowest prices of an entire shopping cart by simultaneously comparing all selected products at multiple suppliers (incl. shipping costs).

The business was acquired in 2014.

positions.title: Intern - Consulting
positions.description:
As an intern, I got a fantastic chance to get an insight look into a merger where David bought Goliath. Back then, the story was all over the press (and quite dramatic). A small automotive manufacturer buys a huge international company and nearly collapses under its debt load. 

After it all worked out fine, we were tasked with improving the organizational structure and reporting system. As an intern, I made a tremendous impact, as you can imagine.

Additionally, I got the chance to directly work with the CFO to analyze how similar family businesses were structuring their company and do their corporate governance. While the task was rather boring, getting to know the CFO (now CEO) and seeing how he works was exciting.

positions.title: Intern - Strategy
positions.description: I developed a new acquisition strategy and supported various sales activities. No, actually, I was just trying to survive with my few words of Spanish. But it was fun.

positions.title: Head - Marketing Ressort
positions.description:
Students are great at distracting themselves from studying. So I decided to lead a team of 25 students to organize Europe's largest finance conference run by students. 

Speakers included: 
 John Forbes Nash, Jr., Nobel Price, Princeton University
 Alexander Dibelius, CEO Germany, Austria, Russia & CEE, Goldman Sachs
 Karl-Georg Altenburg, CEO Germany/Austria/Switzerland, J.P. Morgan

positions.title: Intern - Consulting
positions.description: I was allowed a glimpse into the consulting world, which later hooked me (at least for a while). Here I contributed to a project where we developed a new division for one of our key clients. Also, I helped to find new clients for us.
